# Bot builder instructions

<!-- Generated by build.sh from skills/*/SKILL.md - edit those, then run ./build.sh -->

Follow both parts below in every task on this project.


# Working with this builder

They build Telegram sales bots (VPN shops on Marzban/Rebecca-type panels, with wallets,
gateways, renewals, referrals) and the web panels and installers around them, and they reuse the
same habits on every new bot. They are not a programmer by trade: they judge the result by
using the bot. So results must work when tapped, and explanations must make sense to someone
who sees menus, not code.

## Talking to them

- Reply in **Persian**, fluent and friendly, plain words. Code, file names and commands stay as
  they are.
- Before long work, one line on what you are about to do; while working, a short line now and
  then on what you are doing. No long recaps.
- When something is done: what changed (in their words: which menu, which button), how it was
  tested, what was *not* tested and why, and what they need to do (if anything). Be honest; if
  a voice was synthetic, a payment was only tested against a mock, or a bug might remain, say it.
- Give paths the way they navigate: `🏬 تنظیمات فروشگاه ← 🛒 وضعیت قابلیت‌های فروشگاه ← ⚙️ …`.
- They care about token cost: do not spawn helper agents or re-read huge files without need;
  prefer targeted searches.
- If they answer "اره ولش کن" (forget it), drop that thread completely.
- A decision that is theirs (a repository name, public or private, turning something on by
  default, deleting data) is asked, briefly, with a recommendation. Everything else: decide and do.

## Product taste

- **Everything customizable, per language.** Every customer-facing text and button can be edited
  from the bot's 🎨 menu and from the web panel, separately per language, with premium emoji,
  stickers and button colours. Use the `telegram-bot-customization` skill for how.
- **New features are off by default**, each with its own switch (per language), and with
  sub-switches for the risky parts (for example "keep the gateway's min/max" or "gift on
  direct payment" - both off until the admin turns them on).
- **Every path on its own.** When a bot has several paths (platforms in a downloader, features
  in a shop), each path's captions and buttons are customized separately in 🎨; what is
  really shared is labelled as shared. Details in the `telegram-bot-customization` skill.
- **Three places for every feature:** the bot's admin menu, the web panel, and 🎨. A feature only
  in one of them is not finished.
- **Admin texts are Persian only.** Customer texts exist in every supported language (Persian
  and English); no English inside Persian screens and no Persian left in English ones.
- **Friendly colloquial Persian** in bot texts ("کدوم بخش رو می‌خوای تنظیم کنی؟"), emoji at the
  start of buttons and headings, `<blockquote>` for explanations, `<b>` for amounts and names,
  `<code>` for anything to copy.
- **Telegram behaviour they expect:** move through a flow by editing the same message; the back
  button sits below and returns exactly one step; a toggle flips at once with no confirmation and
  shows its state (✅ green / ❌ red); stale messages are removed; old buttons answer with a clear
  alert; no message silently vanishes; no duplicate messages.
- **Web panel:** dark glass look, Vazirmatn font, right to left, SVG line icons for the panel's
  own chrome, saves without reloading, lists refresh by themselves, date-range filters on every
  list, every ID clickable to the profile, works on a phone, gentle motion (reduced-motion
  respected).
- **Money must be exact:** a purchase, a renewal or a top-up is settled (invoice active, wallet
  changed, payment marked) the moment the external service confirms; a second tap, a second
  approval or a webhook retry never charges, credits or builds twice; failures refund to the
  wallet and say so; min/max limits and gifts follow the admin's settings; every money event is
  reported to the admin group in its topic.
- **📊 Statistics like Ciro:** every bot has «📊 آمار ربات» as the first admin button and the
  same numbers on the web dashboard (details in `telegram-bot-customization`,
  `references/bot-stats.md`); every new paid feature adds its lines there.
- **Updates like Ciro:** when a project needs an update feature, build it the way Ciro does it
  (button in the bot, snapshot first, config and database kept, automatic rollback, progress
  bar in the same message, back to the previous version from the bot, admins told what is
  new). The full design is in the `telegram-bot-customization` skill, `references/self-update.md`.
- **Beginner admins:** after every change set, a "what's new" entry the admin sees in the bot:
  what it is, a concrete example, on/off by default, and the step-by-step path (1️⃣ 2️⃣ 3️⃣),
  plus the web panel path.

## Engineering habits

- Read the code that is there before adding to it; extend the existing mechanism instead of
  creating a second one. Keep compatibility with the original upstream bot and its database
  (an old backup must restore and upgrade itself).
- Database changes are idempotent ("add column if missing") and also applied lazily at first use.
- Test on a local rig before pushing: the real code with a fake Telegram API that logs every
  call, fake panel and gateway APIs, a real database; drive it with scripted taps; crawl the
  menus and read the PHP error log; load every web panel page in a headless browser. Report the
  results, including what failed.
- Debugging means finding the real cause and showing it (the line, the order of operations),
  not adding retries around it. Fix what you can prove; list what you suspect.
- Git: commit with a message that explains why; push to the branches the project uses (often
  the main branch and a working branch together); never force-push; no pull request unless asked;
  do not bump the version number unless asked; never rewrite tags or releases.
- Never weaken security to make something work (no disabled TLS checks, no secrets in code or
  in chat); passwords shown in screenshots or videos are masked.

## Tutorials and media

When they ask for a tutorial video: Persian narration in a natural, warm tone with burned-in
subtitles, section by section with a chapter list, real screens of the bot recorded from the
rig, sensitive values masked. Say plainly if the voice is synthetic and that you could not
listen to it yourself.

# Telegram bot customization (🎨)

The idea in one sentence: **nothing a customer sees is hard-wired.** Every message and every
button has a stable key, a default text per language, and an optional per-language override that
the admin edits from a 🎨 menu inside the bot (and the same data from a web panel). A new feature
is not finished until its texts and buttons are in that system.

This came out of building a large Telegram shop bot (Ciro) where the owner kept asking for "this
should be editable too" one screen at a time. Building it in from the start is far cheaper than
retrofitting 160 messages later, so treat it as part of every feature, not as an extra.

## When you start on a bot

1. Find (or create) the text layer: one file per language with nested keys
   (`users.Balance.shortLine`, `users.sell.service_sell`). No customer text inline in code.
2. Find (or create) the override store and the resolver (see `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/data-model.md`).
3. Find (or create) the registry: the single list that says which keys and button groups appear
   in 🎨, under which group and section, with which admin label.
4. Read `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/checklist.md` before calling any feature done.

If the bot already has some of this under other names, use what exists and extend it. Do not
build a second parallel system.

## The five things that must be editable

| What | Per language | Stored as | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Message text | yes | override text, or none = default | keep placeholders like `{price}` working; HTML or entities |
| Message extras | yes | sticker file_id, reaction emoji, media | sticker is sent before the message and removed when that screen is replaced |
| Buttons of a message | yes | per (message key, button index): name, emoji, premium emoji id, emoji side, plain mode, colour, hidden | back / close buttons can be restyled but never hidden |
| Layout | yes | order of buttons and how many per row | the "📐 چیدمان" editor |
| Feature switches | yes, unless truly global | `feature[lang][key]` | new features default to **off** |

Admin-only texts (the admin menus themselves) do not need per-language overrides; they live in
the admin's language only. Customer texts always exist in every supported language.

## Resolution rules (get these right first)

- `text(key, lang)` = override for (lang, key) if non-empty, else the default text of that
  language, else the default of the primary language. Never return an empty string: Telegram
  refuses empty messages, and a blank bubble looks broken.
- Everything is resolved in the **receiver's** language. A message to a referrer, an approval
  result sent to a customer by an admin, a cron notice: use the recipient's language and their
  overrides, not the language of whoever triggered the request.
- A change on one language tab never changes another language. If something must be shared
  (one payment-processor account for all languages), mark it visibly (🌐) on every tab.
- Buttons are built through one function (`render(def, override, callback)`), so colour, emoji,
  premium emoji and hiding work the same on every screen. Do not hand-build buttons for customer
  screens.
- Overrides are data, never code. Validate on save: placeholders that the default has must still
  be there (warn, do not silently break), HTML must be balanced, length within Telegram limits.

## The 🎨 menu the admin sees

Main screen: language tabs on top (`✅🇮🇷 فارسی | 🇬🇧 English`), then groups. White header buttons
are section titles (tapping one only shows a short alert explaining that section). A green
button means "this item is customized"; a legend explains the markers:
`✏️ text changed  ❤️ has reaction  🖼 has sticker  🔘 buttons changed`. At the bottom:
`🔁 reset all to default` (with confirmation) and `❌ close`.

Item screen (one message):

```
📝 <b>👋 متن خوش‌آمدید</b>
➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖
✏️ متن: پیش‌فرض
🖼 استیکر: ندارد ❌
❤️ ری‌اکشن: ندارد ❌
➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖
👁 <b>متن فعلی:</b>
<blockquote>سلام خوش آمدید</blockquote>
👇 بخشی که می‌خوای تنظیم کنی رو انتخاب کن:
[📋 کپشن پیش‌فرض] [✏️ ویرایش کپشن]
[🖼 استیکر] [❤️ ری‌اکشن]
[🔘 دکمه‌های این پیام]
[🔁 ریست همه‌ی تنظیمات این پیام]
[🔙 بازگشت به منوی قبل] [🔙 برگشت به لیست]
[❌ بستن]
```

Editing a text: the admin sends the new text; premium emoji and formatting are kept (store the
entities or convert them to `<tg-emoji emoji-id="…">` HTML). Show the placeholders this text
supports right in the prompt. After saving, redraw the item screen in place (edit the same
message).

Button screen: list the message's buttons; for each: rename, emoji (normal or premium), emoji
side (start/end), plain (no emoji), colour (`success` green / `danger` red / `primary` blue /
default), hide/show (not for back/close), reset. Show state, not action: a hidden button shows
"🙈 پنهان", not "show".

Layout screen (📐): the buttons in their current rows; tap one to select, then move it
up/down/left/right or change how many sit in a row. Items added later (a new feature button)
must appear in the layout automatically, at a sensible default position, and must be movable.

More detail, including every screen and callback naming, in `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/admin-screens.md`.

## Paths: every path customizable on its own

Most bots have several **paths**: branches that each send their own messages and buttons. A
downloader has one per platform (Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube…); a shop has one per feature
(buy, renew, top-up, my services, test account, hourly account, referral…); a support bot has
one per department. These are examples, not the list: a path is whatever the owner thinks of
as "a part of my bot". The admin must be able to customize each path's captions and buttons
**separately**: the TikTok result can say something different, with different buttons, from
the Instagram one.

- **A path registry.** One list of paths: `id`, admin label with an emoji, per-language
  on/off switch, and the texts and button groups it owns. Adding a path means adding a row; it
  then shows up by itself in 🎨, the web panel, 📐 layout and the feature switches. No path is
  wired into the menus by hand.
- **Keys carry the path.** `dl.instagram.caption`, `dl.tiktok.caption`, `dl.x.caption`; button
  groups too (`dl.tiktok.result_buttons`). Do not reuse one key for several paths just
  because today the text is the same: tomorrow the owner wants it different.
- **Lookup order:** this path's override → the override saved for *all paths* → this path's
  default → the shared default. Every path can be changed alone, and something meant to be
  the same everywhere is still changed once.
- **Know the path at the start of the flow** (from the link, the button, the command) and pass
  it to every text and button lookup of that flow, including messages sent later (a cron, a
  payment callback). Store it with the job or the order when the flow is asynchronous.
- **Say what is shared.** When an item really is one for several paths (the channel link, a
  payment button that appears in five places), the editor says so on screen: "🔗 مشترک بین ۳
  مسیر: اینستاگرام، تیک‌تاک، توییتر". Otherwise it says "📍 فقط برای مسیر تیک‌تاک". The admin
  never has to guess where a change will show.
- **Two shortcuts** on every path item: `📋 کپی از مسیر دیگه` (take another path's text and
  buttons as a start) and `🔗 اعمال روی همهٔ مسیرها` (save as the all-paths override).
- **Default: separate.** Shared only when the thing is genuinely one (and then labelled).

Screens and storage for this: `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/admin-screens.md` (path picker, path group) and
`skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/data-model.md` (registry, keys, resolver).

## Feature switches

- A features screen per scope: "global" (whole bot) and "per language" (this tab only). Each row
  is `[✅ روشن | name]` or `[❌ خاموش | name]`, green/red, and one tap flips it and redraws the
  same message. No confirmation step for a plain on/off.
- Every new feature ships **off**. Turning it on must never change what existing customers see
  until the admin decides.
- A feature with its own settings gets a `⚙️ تنظیمات …` button next to its switch, and its hub
  repeats the language tabs.

## Web panel parity

Whatever the bot's 🎨 can edit, the web panel can edit too, from the same registry and the same
store, so the two never disagree. Pages: texts (group tabs, search, "only customized" filter,
sticker id field), buttons, looks/layout (drag to reorder, live preview), features (cards with
switches). Save without reloading the page (fetch + toast), show the new state immediately. See
`skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/web-panel.md`.

## Telegram UI conventions that go with it

- Edit the current message in place when moving between screens of one flow; send a new message
  only when the old one cannot become the new one (media type change, a sticker in between).
- Remove stale screens (an invoice that was paid, a menu that was replaced) so nothing old can be
  tapped. If an old button is tapped anyway, answer with an alert and a way forward, not a crash
  or a silent no-op.
- Navigation buttons at the bottom: `🔙 back` (red or default), `❌ close`. Confirm buttons green.
- `<blockquote>` for notes and explanations, `<b>` for the values that matter, `<code>` for
  anything the user may copy (IDs, links, amounts).
- Errors and refusals: `answerCallbackQuery` with `show_alert` for short ones; a short message
  with the fix for longer ones. Never "unknown error".
- Every list that can grow: paging, and search when long.

## 📊 Bot statistics

Every bot gets "📊 آمار ربات" as the first admin button, built like Ciro's: language tabs
(each language counted on its own, in its currency), an overall view (users, buyers, tests,
wallets, sales, active sales, renewals, conversion, average per customer, monthly forecast,
renewal share, agents, panels, sales per gateway), period buttons (last hour, today,
yesterday, this month, last month, chosen dates) with count and sum for every paid action,
per-path and per-server numbers, and the same figures on the web panel's dashboard, whose
counters reset to a baseline without deleting anything. Full design and counting rules:
`skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/bot-stats.md`.

## Self-update

If the bot needs an update feature (an admin button that updates the bot, keeps config and
data, snapshots first, rolls back on failure, and announces what is new), build it exactly as
described in `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/self-update.md`: the `version` file, the "🔄 آپدیت ربات" screen,
request files picked up by root's cron watcher, the ten update steps shared with the server's
management command, rollback to a snapshot from the bot, and `whatsnew.php` announced to every
admin in their own language.

## Before you say it is done

Run through `skills/telegram-bot-customization/references/checklist.md`. In short: texts in every language, registry entry, 🎨
item opens and edits, each path customizable on its own, buttons through the shared renderer, switch defaults off, web panel shows
it, receiver-language checked, test on a rig with a fake Telegram API, and a "what's new" note
for the admin that says where to find it (menu path, step by step).

## Reference: Done checklist for any customer-facing change

Copy this into your notes and tick it honestly.

- [ ] Every new customer text exists in **every** language file (no English left in Persian
      screens, no Persian in English ones).
- [ ] Admin-only texts are in the admin language file only.
- [ ] Each new text has a registry entry (label, key, group, section) and opens in 🎨 on every
      language tab; edit, sticker, reaction and reset work.
- [ ] New buttons go through the shared renderer and belong to a button group; rename, emoji,
      premium emoji, colour, hide and layout work; back/close cannot be hidden.
- [ ] The new button shows up in 📐 layout and can be moved.
- [ ] Texts and extras are resolved in the receiver's language (crons, admin actions, referrals).
- [ ] Every path (platform, feature, department…) is in the path registry and has its own 🎨
      group; its texts and buttons open and change without touching the other paths.
- [ ] Keys carry the path; the flow passes the path to every lookup, async messages included.
- [ ] Items that are really shared say so on screen ("🔗 مشترک بین …"), the rest say
      "📍 فقط برای …"; copy-from-path and apply-to-all work.
- [ ] Each path has its own per-language on/off switch.
- [ ] A new feature that sells or is used shows up in 📊 آمار ربات (count and sum, per
      language, per period) and on the web panel's dashboard.
- [ ] A new feature has a switch, per language unless truly global, **off by default**.
- [ ] The web panel can see and change everything the bot can for this feature.
- [ ] Stale buttons from old messages answer with a clear alert, never a PHP/Python error.
- [ ] Money paths are idempotent: a second tap, a second approval or a retried webhook never
      charges, credits or builds twice; state is saved right after the external call succeeds.
- [ ] Tested on a local rig: fake Telegram API that logs calls, fake panel/payment APIs, a real
      database; menus crawled for errors in the log.
- [ ] A what's-new entry for the admin, beginner friendly, with the menu path and the default.

## Reference: Data model

Language-neutral. Any store works (a JSON column, a key-value table, files); what matters is the
shape and the lookup order. The examples use JSON.

## 1. Default texts (in the code base, one file per language)

```php
// lang/fa.php
return [
  'users' => [
    'Balance' => [
      'shortLine' => '💡 برای این خرید <b>{need}</b> کم داری.',
      'directPayGone' => '⛔️ پرداخت مستقیم الان برای این مرحله در دسترس نیست.',
    ],
  ],
];
```

A key is the dotted path: `users.Balance.shortLine`. Keys are stable forever; renaming a key
loses every admin override saved under it, so add a new key instead and migrate.

## 2. Overrides (in the database)

```json
{
  "texts":     { "fa": { "users.Balance.shortLine": "💡 فقط {need} مونده!" }, "en": {} },
  "stickers":  { "fa": { "users.text_start": "CAACAgIAAxkBAA…" } },
  "reactions": { "fa": { "users.text_start": "❤️" } },
  "buttons":   { "fa": { "users.sell.service_sell": { "0": {
                    "text": "بستن", "emoji": "❌", "emojiIcon": "5368324170671202286",
                    "pos": "right", "simple": false, "style": "danger", "hidden": false } } } },
  "layout":    { "fa": { "main_menu": { "order": ["buy","test","services"], "rows": [2,1] } } },
  "features":  { "fa": { "dpay_on": "0", "dpay_limits": "0" }, "en": { "dpay_on": "0" } }
}
```

- `emojiIcon` is a premium (custom) emoji id; Telegram shows it on an inline button through
  `icon_custom_emoji_id`, so the text itself carries no emoji then.
- `style` is the Bot API button colour: `success` (green), `danger` (red), `primary` (blue).
- Missing key = default. An empty string saved by mistake also means default.
- Reset of one item deletes its keys in all five maps for that language only.

## 3. Registry (in the code base)

One list drives the bot's 🎨 menu and the web panel's pages.

```php
'dp_1' => ['label' => '💳 متن مرحلهٔ «پرداخت مستقیم»', 'key' => 'users.Balance.directPayCaption',
           'group' => 'buyflow', 'section' => 'confirm'],
'dp_3' => ['label' => '💰 سرویس این پرداخت قبلاً تحویل شده', 'key' => 'users.Balance.paidInvoiceTaken',
           'group' => 'topup', 'section' => 'topup_done'],
```

- `label` is in the admin's language (it is an admin text).
- `group` = a 🎨 group screen; `section` = a white header inside it.
- Button groups get their own entries (a button group id plus the message key it belongs to).
- An item id is never reused for something else.

## 3b. Paths

```php
// one row per path; menus, web panel tabs, layout and switches are built from this list
'paths' => [
  'instagram' => ['label' => '📸 اینستاگرام', 'switch' => 'dl_instagram_on',
                  'texts' => ['dl.instagram.ask', 'dl.instagram.caption', 'dl.instagram.error'],
                  'buttons' => ['dl.instagram.result_buttons']],
  'tiktok'    => ['label' => '🎵 تیک‌تاک',   'switch' => 'dl_tiktok_on',  …],
  'x'         => ['label' => '🐦 توییتر',    'switch' => 'dl_x_on',       …],
],
```

Overrides keep the normal maps (`texts[lang][key]`, `buttons[lang][key]`…). The all-paths
override of a family of keys is stored under the key with `_all` in the path's place
(`dl._all.caption`), so "apply to every path" is one row, and a path can still override it.

## 4. Resolver

```
function text(key, lang, receiver):
    lang = receiver.lang if receiver else lang
    v = overrides.texts[lang][key]           -> if non-empty: return v
    v = defaults[lang][key]                  -> if non-empty: return v
    return defaults[PRIMARY][key] or key     # never empty
```

With paths, a key `family.path.name` is looked up in this order, stopping at the first
non-empty value:

```
overrides.texts[lang]["family.path.name"]      # this path, changed by the admin
overrides.texts[lang]["family._all.name"]      # all paths, changed by the admin
defaults[lang]["family.path.name"]             # this path's default text
defaults[lang]["family._all.name"]             # the shared default text
```

Buttons, stickers, reactions and layout follow the same chain.

Then, when sending: look up sticker/reaction for the same (lang, key), send the sticker first
(remember its message id so the screen can remove it later), then the text, then set the
reaction. Matching extras to a text by key is far more reliable than matching by content; if a
legacy code base only has the final text at send time, match on the literal segments around the
placeholders.

## 5. Button renderer

```
function render(def, ov, callback):
    text  = ov.text or def.text
    style = ov.style or def.style
    if ov.simple:       text = strip_leading_emoji(text)
    elif ov.emojiIcon:  text = strip_leading_emoji(text); icon = ov.emojiIcon
    elif ov.emoji:      text = place(ov.emoji, strip_leading_emoji(text), ov.pos)
    return {text, callback_data: callback, style, icon_custom_emoji_id: icon}
function visible(def, ov): return not ov.hidden or def.required   # back/close are required
```

## 6. Migrations

Add columns and keys idempotently ("add if missing") at install, at update and lazily at first
use. Never assume an upgrade ran. When the stored shape changes, keep reading the old shape.

## Reference: Admin screens

All admin screens are edited in place (one message that changes), carry the language tabs when
the content is per language, and end with a way back and `❌ بستن`.

## Callback naming

Short, prefixed, `|`-separated, ≤ 64 bytes (Telegram's limit): `bt_edit|fa|users.text_start`,
`btact|sticker|fa|users.text_start`, `gbs|hub|fa|cf`, `dpay|tog|fa|limits`. One dispatcher per
prefix, early in the update handler, returning "handled" so nothing else runs.

## 🎨 main list

```
🎨 <b>شخصی‌سازی پیام‌های ربات</b>
متنی که می‌خواهی تغییر دهی را انتخاب کن.
⬜️ دکمه‌های سفید فقط تیتر بخش‌ان…
🟢 دکمه سبز یعنی این مورد سفارشی شده: ✏️ متن  ❤️ ری‌اکشن  🖼 استیکر  🔘 دکمه‌ها
[✅🇮🇷 فارسی] [🇬🇧 English]
[💬 پیام‌های عمومی ربات]            ← white header (alert only)
[👋 متن خوش‌آمدید] …               ← items, green when customized
[🛒 پیام‌ها و ظاهر مراحل خرید]      ← a group with its own screen
…
[🔁 ریست همه به پیش‌فرض] [❌ بستن]
```

## Group screen

Explains in a short quote what belongs here and any rule ("product has two captions: with and
without categories; only one is active"), then sections and items. Buttons that edit how the
*buttons* of a flow look ("🎨 ظاهر دکمه‌های …") sit under their own header, apart from texts.

## Path picker (when the bot has paths)

One button per path from the path registry, green when anything in it is customized, then the
shared items:

```
🧭 <b>شخصی‌سازی مسیرها</b>
هر مسیر کپشن و دکمه‌های خودش رو داره؛ یکی رو انتخاب کن.
[✅🇮🇷 فارسی] [🇬🇧 English]
[📸 اینستاگرام] [🎵 تیک‌تاک]       ← green = customized
[🐦 توییتر]     [▶️ یوتیوب]
[🔗 تنظیمات مشترک همهٔ مسیرها]
[🔙 بازگشت] [❌ بستن]
```

## Path group

The group screen for one path: its texts (ask for link, waiting, result caption, error), its
button groups, its sticker. Each item shows where a change applies:

```
🎵 <b>تیک‌تاک</b> — 🇮🇷 فارسی
[📝 کپشن نتیجه]   ← 📍 فقط برای تیک‌تاک
[⏳ پیام «در حال دانلود…»]
[❌ پیام خطا]
[🔘 دکمه‌های زیر نتیجه]
[📋 کپی از مسیر دیگه] [🔗 اعمال روی همهٔ مسیرها]
[🔙 مسیرها]
```

On the item screen of a shared item the status block carries one more line:
`🔗 مشترک بین ۳ مسیر: اینستاگرام، تیک‌تاک، توییتر`.

## Item screen

See SKILL.md. Lines that show state: `✏️ متن: پیش‌فرض / سفارشی`, `🖼 استیکر: دارد ✅ / ندارد ❌`,
`❤️ ری‌اکشن: …`, plus a toggle where the item has one (`✅ استیکر خوش‌آمد روشنه`).

## Text edit prompt

```
✏️ متن جدید رو بفرست.
می‌تونی از ایموجی پریمیوم و فرمت تلگرام استفاده کنی.
<blockquote>متغیرها: {price} قیمت · {balance} موجودی</blockquote>
[🔙 انصراف]
```

On a text that lost a placeholder: save it, but say which placeholder is now missing and that
the value will not appear.

## Button group screen

```
🔘 <b>دکمه‌های صفحهٔ تایید خرید</b> — 🇮🇷 فارسی
[✅ تایید و پرداخت از کیف پول]  ← tap = that button's editor
[💳 پرداخت مستقیم]
[🔙 بازگشت]
[📐 چیدمان] [🔁 ریست]
```

Button editor: `✏️ نام`, `😀 ایموجی`, `💎 ایموجی پریمیوم`, `↔️ سمت ایموجی`, `🎨 رنگ: سبز/قرمز/آبی/پیش‌فرض`,
`🙈 پنهان / 👁 نمایان`, `🔁 ریست این دکمه`. Each tap redraws with the new state visible.

## Main menu buttons (reply keyboard)

The fixed main-menu buttons get their own hub: colour (separately for inline "glass" style and
reply keyboard), emoji or a sticker sent on tap, layout (order and width), name and show/hide.
Renaming a reply-keyboard button must keep the handler matching (match by key, not by the text
the admin typed).

## Features hub (per language)

```
📌 <b>وضعیت قابلیت‌های فروشگاه</b>
هر دکمه یه قابلیت رو روشن یا خاموش می‌کنه؛ کافیه روی دکمه‌اش بزنی.
✅ فعال | ❌ غیرفعال
🌐 این تنظیمات برای هر زبان جداست…
[✅🇮🇷 فارسی] [🇬🇧 English]
[❌ 🔋 وضعیت حجم اضافه]
[✅ 💳 دکمهٔ «پرداخت مستقیم» در صفحهٔ تایید]
[⚙️ تنظیمات پرداخت مستقیم]
```

## What's-new screen

A list of short entries the admin sees after an update: what changed, an example, whether it is
on or off by default, and the exact path (`1️⃣ 🏬 تنظیمات فروشگاه ← 2️⃣ … ← 3️⃣ …`) plus the web
panel path. Written for a beginner.

---

## Reference: Web panel

The panel is a second door to the same data; it never has settings the bot cannot reach, and
the bot never has settings the panel cannot reach (except things that only make sense in chat).

## Pages that mirror 🎨

- **Texts**: group tabs from the registry, a search box, "only customized" filter, per item a
  textarea with the current text, the default shown beside it, a sticker file_id field, a reset
  link. Language tabs at the top.
- **Paths**: when the bot has paths, the texts and buttons pages get path tabs (one per path
  in the registry, plus "همهٔ مسیرها") under the language tabs; each item says whether it is
  path-only or shared, and has "copy from path" and "apply to all paths".
- **Buttons / looks**: per button group, rows of name / emoji / colour / side / hidden; a live
  preview of the keyboard; drag to reorder; row width.
- **Features**: cards per feature with switches; a feature's settings inside its card.
- **Lists** (users, orders, payments, services): date-range filter with presets (today, 7 days,
  30 days, custom from–to), search, paging, every ID clickable to the profile.

## Behaviour

- Save without reloading (fetch/AJAX), toast "ذخیره شد", the new state drawn at once; a new item
  appears without a manual refresh.
- Works on a phone: no sideways scroll, touch scrolling inside tables and long lists.
- Right-to-left for Persian, a Persian font (Vazirmatn), numbers formatted.
- The panel's own chrome uses line icons (SVG), not emoji; emoji stay where they are the bot's
  content (a button text the admin set).
- Motion is short and purposeful; respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Log in with a username and password generated by the bot; the bot can reset them.

## Reference: Bot statistics: "📊 آمار ربات" (build it like Ciro's)

Every bot built with this skill gets an admin statistics screen, the first button of the admin
menu, and the same numbers on the web panel's dashboard. Below is Ciro's design, written
generally: "order" is whatever the bot sells or does (a subscription, a download, a booking),
"path" is a platform or feature (see Paths in SKILL.md).

## The screen

- Language tabs on top (`✅🇮🇷 فارسی | 🇬🇧 English`): each language's users, sales and wallets
  are counted on their own, in that language's currency. A rate between languages is never
  mixed into one total.
- Opens on the overall view; the buttons under it switch the period by editing the same
  message:

```
[✅🇮🇷 فارسی] [🇬🇧 English]
[⏱️ آمار کل]
[⏱️ یک ساعت اخیر]
[⛅️ امروز] [☀️ دیروز]
[☀️ ماه فعلی] [⛅️ ماه قبل]
[🗓 مشاهده آمار در تاریخ مشخص]      ← asks for a from-date and a to-date (Jalali for Persian)
```

## Overall view (Ciro's text)

```
🌐 آمار کاربران و فروش زبان: <b>🇮🇷 فارسی</b>
📊 <b>آمار کلی ربات</b>
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
👥 <b>تعداد کل کاربران:</b> <code>1,240</code> نفر
💳 <b>کاربران دارای خرید:</b> <code>310</code> نفر
🧪 <b>اکانت‌های تست:</b> <code>95</code> نفر
💰 <b>موجودی کل کاربران:</b> <code>4,200,000 تومان</code>

🧾 <b>تعداد کل فروش:</b> <code>620</code> عدد
🧾 <b>تعداد کل فروش سرویس های فعال:</b> <code>280</code> عدد
💵 <b>جمع کل فروش :</b> <code>93,000,000 تومان</code>
💵 <b>جمع کل فروش سرویس های فعال:</b> <code>42,000,000 تومان</code>
🔄 <b>جمع کل تمدید:</b> <code>18,500,000 تومان</code>
📈 <b>نرخ تبدیل به مشتری:</b> <code>25</code>٪
💳 <b>میانگین خرید هر مشتری:</b> <code>135,000 تومان</code>
📅 <b>درآمد پیش‌بینی‌شده ماهانه:</b> <code>36,000,000 تومان</code>
📊 <b>درصد تمدید از فروش:</b> <code>44</code>٪

👨‍💼 <b>تعداد کل نمایندگان:</b> <code>12</code> نفر
🔹 <b>نمایندگان نوع N:</b> <code>9</code> نفر
🔸 <b>نمایندگان نوع N2:</b> <code>3</code> نفر
🧩 <b>تعداد پنل‌ها:</b> <code>5</code> عدد
💳 کارت به کارت: 410 عدد · 61,000,000 تومان       ← one line per gateway that was used
```

How each number is made:
- **buyers:** distinct users with at least one paid order. **Conversion:** buyers ÷ users.
- **Average per customer:** active sales ÷ buyers.
- **Monthly forecast:** yesterday's sales × 30.
- **Renewal share:** renewals ÷ active sales, capped at 100.
- **Per gateway:** paid payments only. Manual credits by an admin are not income and are left
  out.

Lines for the bot's other paid features are appended the same way (Ciro adds a line for its
hourly accounts).

## A period (one hour, today, yesterday, this month, last month, chosen dates)

```
🕐 <b>آمار روز فعلی</b>
⏳ بازه تایم  : 1405/08/16 00:00 تا 1405/08/16 14:20

🛍 تعداد سفارشات : 18 عدد
💸 جمع مبلغ سفارشات  : 2,700,000 تومان
🧲 تعداد تمدید  : 7 عدد
💰 جمع مبلغ تمدید: 1,050,000 تومان
📦 حجم‌های اضافه  : 3 عدد · 💰 210,000 تومان
⏱️ زمان‌های اضافه  : 1 عدد · 💰 60,000 تومان
📍 تغییر لوکیشن  : 0 عدد · 💰 0 تومان
🔑 اکانت‌های تست  : 11 عدد
👤 تعداد کاربران  : 26 نفر                     ← new users in the period
```

Every paid action the bot sells gets its own pair of lines: count and sum.

## Counting rules

- Unpaid invoices never count; test accounts are counted on their own line, never as sales.
- A period includes both ends; store times as unix timestamps (convert legacy text dates
  once in the query).
- Queries take parameters, never string-built values. Per-language filtering is one shared
  helper (where-clause + params) used by every query, so the tabs always agree.
- With paths: a per-path block (uses and sales of each platform or feature) under the totals,
  in the registry's order.

## Per panel / server

On each panel's management screen: connection state, number and sum of sales on that panel,
user group. Shows the admin at once which server sells and which one is down.

## Web panel dashboard

- **Cards:**
  - کل کاربران
  - درآمد کل (each currency on its own line)
  - سرویس فعال
  - پرداخت در انتظار, with a link to them
- **Two short tables:** latest orders and latest users, every ID clickable to the profile.
- **Filters:**
  - a language filter (همه / each language with its count)
  - a date-range filter: today, 7 days, 30 days, custom from-to
- **Resetting counters.** Buttons to reset the dashboard's income, today's transactions and
  active-services counters. A reset stores a *baseline* (a start time or offset) and the cards
  count from there; it never deletes payments or orders, so the bot's own statistics and every
  report stay complete. Each reset asks once to confirm and can be undone.

## Reference: Self-update: "🔄 آپدیت ربات" (build it exactly like this)

When a bot project needs an update feature, build this design, from the Ciro bot. The owner
updates from a button in the bot, sees a progress bar in the same message, never loses
config or data, can go back to the previous version from the bot, and every admin is told
what changed. The same steps also run from the server's management command, so there is
**one** update path, not two.

## Pieces

| Piece | Where | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `version` file | repo root, one line (`1.0.4`) | the installed version; compared with the same file on the main branch |
| Update screen | bot: ⚙️ تنظیمات عمومی ← 🔄 آپدیت ربات | shows versions and state, starts an update or a rollback |
| Request files | the bot's own directory | how the bot (web user) asks root to act |
| Root watcher | cron, every minute: `* * * * * flock -n /tmp/<cmd>_selfupdate.lock /usr/local/bin/<cmd> selfupdate-watch` | picks up requests and runs the real update |
| Management command | `/usr/local/bin/<cmd>` (the installer itself, e.g. `Ciro`) | menu with install / update / backup / restore; `<cmd> update` is the same code the watcher runs |
| `table.php` (migrations) | repo root | only creates missing tables and adds missing columns; safe to run any time |
| `whatsnew.php` | repo root | history of release notes, announced to admins once after each update |

## Why the split

The bot runs as the web-server user and cannot replace its own files or restart anything. So
it never updates itself directly: it writes a small request file in its directory, and root's
watcher (installed by the installer as one crontab line, added once and matched by its command
text) does the work within a minute. Everything that crosses from the bot to root is validated
on both sides (fixed file names, snapshot names matched against a strict pattern).

## The update screen

```
<blockquote><b>🔄 آپدیت ربات</b>
🤖 @botname</blockquote>

نسخه فعلی: <b>1.0.4</b>
آخرین به‌روزرسانی: <b>1405/08/16 14:20</b>      ← Jalali for Persian, Gregorian otherwise

✅ <b>آخرین نسخه را داری</b>                     ← or: 🆕 <b>نسخهٔ جدید آماده است: 1.0.5</b>
تاریخ آخرین تغییرات: <b>2026-11-07</b>           ← date of the last whatsnew entry

<blockquote>✅ تنظیمات، دیتابیس، پنل‌ها و فایل config دست‌نخورده می‌مانند. پیش از شروع یک بکاپ
کامل گرفته می‌شود و اگر آپدیت به مشکل بخورد، ربات خودکار به همین نسخه برمی‌گردد.</blockquote>

[🚀 شروع آپدیت]                 ← primary; on the latest version: [🔁 نصب دوباره‌ی همین نسخه] (success)
[♻️ بازگشت به نسخه قبلی]        ← danger; only when snapshots exist
```

- The latest version is read from the raw `version` file on the main branch, cached for 10
  minutes; a failed read is retried after one minute and the old value is kept meanwhile.
- The start button stays on the latest version too ("reinstall"), because a push without a
  version bump must still be installable.
- While a job is pending or running, no buttons: one line "⏳ یک کار در جریان است. همین پیام
  خودش به‌روز می‌شود." A failed run shows its reason.
- "♻️ بازگشت به نسخه قبلی" opens a list of this bot's snapshots with their dates; picking one
  asks once to confirm, then writes the rollback request. A callback carries only the snapshot's
  date stamp (Telegram limits callback data to 64 bytes); the bot maps it back to the name.

## Request and status files (in the bot directory)

- `update_request` / `rollback_request` (with the snapshot name): the ask. The watcher claims
  one by renaming it to `*.running`; a claim older than 30 minutes is treated as dead and
  removed, so the screen can never stay "busy" for ever after a crash or reboot.
- A context file written by the bot **in the admin's language**: chat id, message id, and the
  three texts the watcher will put into that message (progress, done, failed) with
  placeholders `{bar}`, `{percent}`, `{backup}`. The watcher is a shell script and knows no
  languages; it only fills placeholders.
- `update_status.json`: `{state: running|done|failed|restored|stale, detail, at}` for the
  screen. `update_backups.json`: this bot's snapshots, newest first.
- A busy check covers all of them: a second request is never written over the first, and an
  update and a rollback are never asked for at the same time.

## The steps (identical from the bot and from `<cmd> update`)

0. Find the bot and its current version. An install of the original upstream project (same
   config variables, no `version` file) is upgraded in place. Confirm once (the bot already
   confirmed before writing the request).
1. **Snapshot first.** `tar.gz` of the bot directory without logs, `.git`, backups and the
   request/status files, named `pre-update_<botusername>_<YYYYmmdd>_<HHMMSS>.tar.gz`. Keep the
   newest two per bot; never touch another bot's. If the snapshot fails, stop: nothing changed.
2. **Download** the target archive; check the essential files are in it; delete any packaged
   `config.php` so real credentials are never overwritten.
3. **Dependencies** (composer, npm, pip...) are installed in the extracted copy first, so a
   failure there changes nothing on the live bot.
4. **Overlay** the new files onto the bot directory (copy over, never wipe), so whatever the
   operator added (config, uploads, vendor, custom files) stays. Fix ownership and permissions.
5. **Syntax-check** the core files (`php -l` or the language's equivalent). Any failure:
   restore the snapshot automatically and report "update failed, previous version restored".
6. **Migrate the database additively** (`table.php`: create missing tables, add missing
   columns, fill defaults; never drop or rename). If it cannot run from the shell, try its URL;
   if that fails too, say so and tell the admin to open it once.
7. Repair only what is missing in the web server config; never overwrite a customized vhost.
8. Check that the bot answers.
9. Refresh the management command itself and make sure the watcher's cron line exists.
10. **Tell every admin, in their own language**: "✅ ربات آپدیت شد", the bot's @username, the
    domain, the new version, the time (Jalali | Gregorian), where the previous version's
    snapshot is, and under it every what's-new entry they have not seen yet.

During the run the watcher edits the admin's same message with a progress bar
(`▰▰▰▱▱▱  45٪`) and, at the end, the done or failed text. A rollback follows the same steps
with its own texts ("♻️ در حال بازگشت به نسخه قبلی…", "✅ ربات به نسخه قبلی برگشت.").

## What's new (`whatsnew.php`)

```php
return [
  ['n' => 76, 'date' => '2026-11-07',
   'fa' => "<blockquote>🛠 <b>…title…</b>\n…what changed, an example, on/off by default,\n1️⃣ menu ← 2️⃣ … ← 3️⃣ …\n🌐 پنل وب: …</blockquote>",
   'en' => "<blockquote>…</blockquote>"],
];
```

- A history, oldest first; every change set **adds** one entry with the next `n`. An admin who
  skipped updates is told every entry they missed, in order. Drop the oldest beyond ~15.
- `storage/whatsnew_seen` keeps the last `n` announced. `table.php` announces what is pending,
  once, at the end of each migration; a fresh install starts as "seen" instead of sending the
  whole history.
- Each entry is written for a beginner: what it is, a concrete example, whether it is on or off
  by default, the exact path in the bot step by step, and the web panel path.
- The version number is bumped only when the owner releases; pushing code alone does not bump it.

## Several bots on one server

A registry of installed bots (directory, username, domain). The watcher walks every bot
directory; each bot only ever updates or rolls back itself, and snapshots are named after
their bot.
